Dr. Patel: Good morning, come on in. This must be Bella. What's been going on with her?
Owner: Good morning. Yes, this is Bella, she's a four-year-old Labrador. She's been shaking her head and scratching at her ears for about two weeks now, mostly the left one. Last weekend I noticed a brown, smelly discharge on the inside of the flap.
Dr. Patel: Okay. Has she had ear trouble before?
Owner: She had one infection last summer after we went to the lake a lot. It cleared up with drops. This time it seems worse, she yelped when I touched it yesterday.
Dr. Patel: Is she itchy anywhere else, like paws or belly? Any licking at her feet?
Owner: Yes, she licks her paws a lot, especially in the spring. Her belly gets a bit pink too. Her appetite is fine and she's drinking normally. She hasn't vomited and her energy is good.
Dr. Patel: What do you feed her, and is she on any medications or flea prevention?
Owner: She eats a chicken-based kibble. She takes her monthly heartworm and flea chewable, I gave it on time. No other medications.
Dr. Patel: Great. Let me have a look. She weighs 32 kilograms today, which is about the same as last year. Temperature is 101.6 Fahrenheit, heart rate 96 beats per minute, respiratory rate 24 breaths per minute. Body condition is 5 out of 9. Mucous membranes are pink and moist, capillary refill under two seconds.
Dr. Patel: Heart and lungs sound normal. Abdomen is soft. Skin shows mild erythema in the axillae and between the toes. Now the ears. The right ear canal looks mildly pink with a little wax but the eardrum is visible. The left ear canal is red, swollen and narrowed, with a lot of dark brown waxy exudate, and she's painful when I handle it. I can't see the eardrum on the left.
Owner: Is that bad?
Dr. Patel: I took a swab for cytology from both ears. Under the microscope the left ear has lots of yeast, the Malassezia type, and a moderate number of rod-shaped bacteria. The right ear has just a few yeast. So I suspect a left otitis externa with a yeast and bacterial infection, and I suspect an underlying allergy, likely environmental or food related, because of the paws and the belly and last year's infection.
Dr. Patel: My recommendation is to gently flush the left ear with a cleaner today, then start an ear medication containing an antibiotic, an antifungal and a steroid, five drops in the left ear twice daily for fourteen days. I'd also like to start a pain relief tablet, and I'll dispense carprofen, but let me confirm the dose with the technician before it goes in the bag.
Owner: Okay. Should I clean it at home too?
Dr. Patel: Use the cleaner once daily before the drops, and do not use cotton swabs. Keep her out of the water until the recheck. We'll recheck both ears in two weeks, and book a time then to discuss an allergy work-up or a food trial. If she gets worse, head tilt, loss of balance or swelling, call us right away.
Owner: That all makes sense. Let's book the recheck for two weeks from today.
